candidates.why: bit_write_BL calls bit_write_BB (line 592/596/599); inside bit_write_BB, line 220 writes dat->chain[dat->byte] and then line 222 calls bit_chain_alloc which reallocs (frees) dat->chain at line 3015. The buffer written at 220 is the pre-realloc buffer; any pointer cached into it before line 222 would dangle. Suspicious because the free (3015) and the earlier write (220) are in different functions reached from bit_write_BL.

bit_write_BL calls bit_write_BB at line 592, which may realloc/free dat->chain via bit_chain_alloc (line 211 or 222 -> free at 3015). Immediately after, line 593 calls bit_write_RL which re-accesses dat->chain. If a caller of bit_write_BL held a raw pointer into dat->chain across the call, it is used after the free. Cross-function free/use.

bit_write_BL calls bit_write_BB at line 599 (may realloc/free dat->chain at 3015), then line 600 calls bit_write_RC which reads/writes dat->chain (lines 357-362). A pointer into the old buffer captured before the realloc would be used after free.

In bit_write_RC (reached from bit_write_BL line 600), the while loop at 355-356 calls bit_chain_alloc (realloc/free at 3015); line 357 reads dat->chain[dat->byte] and line 359 writes dat->chain[dat->byte]. If dat->byte+1 was already < dat->size the loop does not run, but if it did run the buffer is reallocated between the guard and the write — re-indexed so likely safe, but flagged as suspicious.
